questions.prompt: Are arrays covariant or contravariant in their element type?

options.text: Covariant — a Dog[] is usable as an Animal[] because Dog is a subtype of Animal
Contravariant — an Animal[] is usable as a Dog[]

questions.explanation: Containers and outputs are covariant: since Dog is a subtype of Animal, a Dog[] can be used where an Animal[] is expected.

questions.prompt: Why can a `Handler<Animal>` be used where a `Handler<Dog>` is expected?

options.text: Function parameters are contravariant — a handler that accepts any Animal can safely accept a Dog
It cannot be used that way

questions.explanation: Parameters are contravariant: a function accepting the wider type (Animal) safely stands in where the narrower input (Dog) is needed.

questions.prompt: What does a `const` type parameter do?

options.text: Makes the parameter readonly at runtime
Infers the narrowest type for the argument (as if `as const` were written), preserving literal types

questions.explanation: A const type parameter (TypeScript 5.0) infers the narrowest, literal-preserving type — so callers get precise types without writing as const.

questions.prompt: For `pair<T>(a: T, b: T)`, what is T when you call `pair(1, 'a')`?

options.text: string | number — the best common type across both argument positions

questions.explanation: T appears in both arguments, so TypeScript infers the best common type across them — here the union string | number.

questions.prompt: The strict option that makes function-parameter checking sound (contravariant) is strict______Types. (one word to complete)
questions.explanation: strictFunctionTypes checks function-type parameters contravariantly, catching unsafe substitutions the loose rules would allow.

questions.prompt: How do you guarantee a value matches the specific key it's set on?

options.text: Constrain with K extends keyof T and type the value as T[K]
Use a union of all value types

questions.explanation: K extends keyof T plus a value typed T[K] ties the value type to the chosen key, so mismatches are impossible.
